quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Rely on your mirrors.
Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change when driving on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles often hide in your blind spot. Look over your shoulder before you change lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes or turning on a residential street. Signal 5 seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: A driver should watch carefully for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians because:

options.text: They're difficult to see in traffic.
They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.
They always have the right-of-way.
They don't have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They're difficult to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many drivers have missed motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians even while looking. These road users are harder to spot because they are smaller, move faster, and have less visible lights. Always watch for motorcycles, bikes, and pedestrians to prevent crashes.

questions.question: What kinds of drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold remedies
All of these choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these choices
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medications. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes:

options.text: Look into the left side mirror.
Look into the right side mirror.
Look into the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Accelerate quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is especially dangerous on slippery roads when taking turns or curves. Slow down more than usual when turning on slippery roads.

questions.question: Increase your following distance when:

options.text: Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.
Exiting an expressway.
Following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles that block your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When in a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.
Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Go to the next turn or exit instead.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive to a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle, the driver of a small vehicle must be prepared for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wind gusts produced by the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Be ready to steer correctly when approaching or passing large vehicles moving at high speeds.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can turn minor injuries into serious ones. Keep the injured person warm while waiting for help. If there is heavy bleeding, press directly on the wound to stop it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Roundabout ahead.
No passing zone.
Left turn yield on green.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Maintain
Vary
Reduce

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you stay in control, keep your car in your lane, and react to problems.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Call the police right away.
Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Flash your headlights to show the driver they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back to the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get away from them. Trying to get even makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not panic. Let off the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road. Keep both hands on the wheel and turn gently into the right lane. Check for traffic before steering back onto the road.

questions.question: What should you do when someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This lets the tailgater pass you.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, move to the right lane if possible. If no right lane exists, wait for clear road ahead and slow down gradually. This encourages the other driver to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Steer too far in the opposite direction.
Turn your wheel toward traffic.
Turn your wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheel in the direction the vehicle is skidding.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: When can you go through a stop sign with no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for cross traffic.
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.
After slowing to 10 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe.
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at any intersection with a stop sign. If there is a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Go only when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean on a regulatory sign?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
An action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drive slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that forbid actions are rectangular, white, red, and black. A red circle with a slash over a symbol means that action is forbidden.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Stick part of your car onto the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to blend in with traffic.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
questions.explanation: Do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see all tracks clearly. Another train may be coming on a different track.

questions.question: What does this sign prevent?

options.text: Entry to full parking lots.
Entry to road construction areas.
Entry to dead-end streets.
Entry from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entry from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic flows in one direction only. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep tires filled to the correct air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a vehicle slides on water between the tires and road. Low air pressure, worn tread, and speeding all increase hydroplaning risk.

questions.question: When can you drive in an HOV lane?

options.text: When you are driving faster than other traffic.
When you are driving slower than other traffic.
When your vehicle has more than one person in it.
When you need to get somewhere quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle has more than one person in it.
questions.explanation: HOV (High Occupancy Vehicle) lanes are reserved for vehicles with multiple passengers. These lanes are marked with signs and diamond symbols on the pavement.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots regularly.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for conditions. Always follow speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.
